findings.title: ConsumeMemoShareView test omits the nonexistent-id and zero-limit edges
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate sqlite ConsumeMemoShareView (store/db/sqlite/memo_share.go:184) from `rows == 1` to `rows >= 0`, or drop the `view_count < view_limit` guard for limit 0. TestMemoShareViewLimitConsumption still passes for the cases it covers, but a consume of a deleted or unknown share id would return true, so a revoked link could be reported as claimed. A share with limit 0 is never exercised.
findings.evidence: store/test/memo_share_test.go:214-236 only consumes a limit-2 share and an unlimited share. There is no call with an id that does not exist, and no ViewLimit=0 case. Playbook rule P9: edge cases for changed behaviour.
findings.fix: Add assertions that ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, 99999) returns (false, nil), and that a share created with ViewLimit=0 returns false on its first consume with ViewCount still 0.
findings.verification_note: Traced the scenario against store/db/sqlite/memo_share.go:174-184 and the test at store/test/memo_share_test.go:196-237. The mutants the finding names would not survive the existing test. With `rows >= 0`, the third consume of the exhausted limit-2 share (lines 219-221) affects 0 rows, the mutant returns true, and `require.False(t, ok)` at line 221 fails. Dropping the `view_count < view_limit` guard does the same thing: the third consume would update a row and return true, and line 221 fails. The WHERE clause treats limit 0 the same way as any other limit (`view_count < view_limit`), so a limit-0 share and an exhausted limit-2 share go through the same path. A nonexistent id also gives RowsAffected == 0, the same result line 221 already pins. No plausible mutant of this single conditional UPDATE returns true for an unknown id or a zero limit but false for an exhausted share, so the claim that the test still passes has no concrete wrong outcome behind it. P9 could not be checked: the context pack does not include the playbook section and contains no P9 entry, and its acceptance criteria only require the limit-2, unlimited and list cases, which the test covers. Adding the two extra assertions would be good hygiene, but the failure scenario as written is refuted.

result.notes:
All three drivers now store view_limit and view_count. Create inserts view_limit when set, and list and get select both columns. ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, id) (bool, error) runs 1 conditional UPDATE ("... SET view_count = view_count + 1 WHERE id = ? AND (view_limit IS NULL OR view_count < view_limit)") and returns true only when exactly 1 row changed. Migrations are store/migration/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/26.10/00__add_memo_share_view_limit.sql, and each driver's LATEST.sql has the same columns. A fresh install now records schema 26.10.1. Two existing tests changed for that: TestFreshInstall now expects 26.10.1, and the calver-newer guardrail case now uses 26.10.2. Test added: TestMemoShareViewLimitConsumption in store/test/memo_share_test.go. `DRIVER=sqlite go test ./store/...` passes. The MySQL and PostgreSQL SQL was not run. In the slice gate, the `prove` step only built the area (nit area.build-only), so it did not run the tests against the pre-change tree. I ran the new test directly and it passes.

findings.title: No test pins that the chosen view limit is sent on create (req-panel-choice)
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose someone later deletes `viewLimit: getViewLimit(viewLimit)` at MemoSharePanel.tsx:128, deletes `viewLimit,` at useMemoShareQueries.ts:41, or breaks getViewLimit at MemoSharePanel.tsx:16-18. All 3 tests in memo-share-panel.test.tsx still pass, because they only call formatViewCount. A user could then pick 1 view and get an unlimited link, and no test would catch it. The current code sends the limit correctly, so the outcome today is a regression nothing would catch, not wrong behaviour.
findings.evidence: web/tests/memo-share-panel.test.tsx:3 imports only formatViewCount. Lines 12-26 hold the only describe block, `describe("formatViewCount"`, with 3 cases. No test renders MemoSharePanel, calls useCreateMemoShare or mocks memoServiceClient.createMemoShare. The untested code is the getViewLimit mapping at MemoSharePanel.tsx:16-18, the handleCreate call at :128, and the hook at useMemoShareQueries.ts:38-43, which puts viewLimit into the MemoShare sent to createMemoShare. The ledger entry shows the task covers req-panel-choice.
findings.fix: Add a test that mocks memoServiceClient.createMemoShare, renders the panel (or calls the hook), picks "10 views" and creates. Assert the request memoShare.viewLimit is 10, and that it is unset for "no limit".
findings.verification_note: I read the test file, MemoSharePanel.tsx and useMemoShareQueries.ts in the worktree. The test file has only formatViewCount tests (lines 12-26), and nothing covers getViewLimit, handleCreate or the hook's viewLimit field. So each mutation the finding names would leave the suite green, which confirms the coverage gap. The current code is correct, though. getViewLimit maps "none" to undefined and the other options through Number(), handleCreate passes the result, and the hook sets it on the MemoShare it sends. No user hits a wrong outcome today, so I lowered the finding to no-harm-yet (minor). It is not defect-narrow-trigger. Context: the plan's Acceptance for this task only asks for the view-count text test, but the task's covers list includes req-panel-choice, so a test for that choice is still missing.

result.notes:
Exported `formatViewCount(share: MemoShare, t): string` from MemoSharePanel.tsx; "3 of 10 views" when viewLimit set, else "3 views". `useCreateMemoShare` mutate takes `{ memoName, expireTime?, viewLimit? }`. en.json keys under memo.share: view-count, view-count-limited, views-unlimited, views-1, views-10, views-100. The first gate run was RED with "could not start /bin/sh" (sandbox fault); rerun with sandbox disabled was GREEN. The slice gate only builds web, so the tests ran locally via vitest (3 pass), and pnpm lint passed.

findings.title: FailedResolveDoesNotCount only exercises the expiry early-return, not the consume-last ordering
findings.failure_scenario: Move the ConsumeMemoShareView call in GetSharedMemo (memo_share_service.go:221) to just after getActiveMemoShare (line 183-186), before the memo fetch at line 188. An archived, SPACE-audience, unreadable or creator-missing memo then increments view_count and uses up the limit while returning NotFound. TestMemoShareViewLimit_FailedResolveDoesNotCount still passes, because its only failure is an expired share. isMemoShareExpired fails inside getActiveMemoShare (line 244) before any consume code runs.
findings.evidence: Test lines 480-487 set expires_ts in the past with raw SQL, then assert NotFound and ViewCount 0. memo_share_service.go:220 says 'Consume last so any failed resolve above leaves the count untouched', but no test reaches the later failure returns: line 193-194 (archived, missing or SPACE memo), line 197-198 (read context denied) and line 215-216 (creator not found). The pack's assumption says the view is consumed only after 'token found, not expired, memo readable'.
findings.fix: Add a case that creates a limited share, archives the memo (as TestGetSharedMemo_ReturnsNotFoundForArchivedMemo does), resolves it, and asserts NotFound and ViewCount==0 and ViewLimit remaining usable. Keep the expiry case too.
findings.verification_note: Traced GetSharedMemo. getActiveMemoShare returns NotFound for an expired share at line 244, before the memo fetch (188) and the consume (221). So the test cannot tell consume-last from consume right after getActiveMemoShare, and the suggested mutation would survive. The production code is correct today: consume runs after every check. The PLAN acceptance only asked for the expiry case, so the gap is in guarding a stated property, not a wrong outcome anyone sees. That is why I lowered it to minor under no-harm-yet: the reproduced impact is a regression the suite would miss, not a current failure.

findings.title: View-limit boundary values 1 and 1000 are never asserted as accepted
findings.failure_scenario: Change the check at memo_share_service.go:69 from `limit > 1000` to `limit >= 1000`. TestCreateMemoShare_RejectsViewLimitOutOfRange only tries 0, -1 and 1001, so it still passes, and a user asking for exactly 1000 views is rejected.
findings.evidence: Test line 418: `for _, limit := range []int32{0, -1, 1001}`. The accepted values elsewhere are 1 (line 431) and 5 (line 474). No test creates a share with 1000.
findings.fix: Add a positive case creating a share with ViewLimit 1000 and assert success and GetViewLimit()==1000.
findings.verification_note: Confirmed that service line 69 is `if limit < 1 || limit > 1000`. The lower boundary 1 is covered as accepted by TestMemoShareViewLimit_ResolvesOnceThenNotFound (line 431-435), so an off-by-one there would be caught. The upper boundary 1000 is never accepted in any test, so a `>= 1000` mutation survives. The current code is correct, so the severity stays minor under no-harm-yet. I moved the line to 418, which holds the value list; 417 is the func declaration. | reviewer cited line 417, verifier traced line 418

result.notes:
CreateMemoShare rejects view_limit outside 1..1000 with INVALID_ARGUMENT and stores it. GetSharedMemo calls Store.ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, ms.ID) last, after memo conversion succeeds; false returns NOT_FOUND "not found". convertMemoShareFromStore sets ViewLimit and ViewCount. Tests: TestCreateMemoShare_RejectsViewLimitOutOfRange, TestMemoShareViewLimit_ResolvesOnceThenNotFound, TestMemoShareViewLimit_UnlimitedShareCountsWithoutLimit, TestMemoShareViewLimit_FailedResolveDoesNotCount. DRIVER=sqlite go test ./server/api/v1/... passes. Slice prove only built the area (nit area.build-only); I did not confirm the new tests fail against the old code.
